evaluations.label: A
errors: Next step says the 'working design presentation' is not yet on the server and should be saved from email; in the transcript the industrial designer's working design presentation was already in the shared folder, and it was the project manager's own file that was missing.
'channel-zapping ~65% of use time' misstates the finding that people zap about 65% during an hour of use.
'submit before individual work session' for the questionnaire and summary is not stated in the transcript.
The locator is described as a 'button on TV'. This was only the project manager's suggestion, and the group agreed to want something to prevent loss.
strengths: Covers the market numbers, the technical components, the infrared choice, the cradle idea and the price points (25 euro retail, 12.50 production) correctly.
Correctly shows the target group as not fixed to an age band, with simplicity and fashion as the emphasis.
Captures the agreed functions, the corporate colors, the TV-only scope and the no-teletext requirement.
Includes the individual workstreams and the marketing expert's promise to email more age data.
weaknesses: The action items are generic, have no owners, and one of them is wrong.
The project manager's own follow-ups are missing: put the minutes and slides in project documentation, and sort out the missing presentation.
No indication of who said what.

evaluations.label: B
errors: 'Management decided against including teletext support or voice recognition': only teletext was a management decision; voice recognition was dismissed by the team on cost and need.

The 'Unresolved Questions' (would the beep function fit the budget, whether a rechargeable system doubles as storage, whether advanced features fit the cost limit) were not raised that way in the meeting. The find-it function was agreed.
Speaker numbers (Speaker 2/3/4/5) are used inconsistently, and the notes say Speaker 2 'emphasized' corporate identity, so the reader cannot tell who is who.
The 'under 65' and 'teenagers and families' target remarks are presented as a discussion of ages 15-35 versus broad appeal, which blurs what was actually proposed.
Action Items section says '(none)' although the meeting ended with explicit follow-ups.
strengths: Clear outline of the meeting's sections, with the research numbers and technical components right.
Gets the cost limit, the 25 euro price, the infrared choice and the cradle idea right.
weaknesses: No action items, even though the meeting closed with individual assignments, a questionnaire and summary, and the project manager's follow-ups.
Contains invented open questions and a misattributed decision.
Anonymous speaker numbers cut its usefulness for someone who missed the meeting.

evaluations.label: C
errors: Several timestamps are approximate or slightly off (for example the 15:20 working-design marker and the 32:02 and 34:48 markers).
Action items name only the project manager's follow-ups ('Speaker 1') and omit the marketing expert's promise to email further age data.
strengths: Reports the target market as open, consistent with the transcript, and records the age ranges suggested (15-35, under 65, 20-55) and the alternative of defining by income.

Gives the reasoning behind decisions: voice recognition against the 12.50 production ceiling and 25 euro price, the hatch or slide idea for secondary buttons, and the check that it does not impede the chip.
Includes owned action items (add the minutes and slides to project documentation; resolve where the project manager's presentation is saved).
Covers the individual assignments, the questionnaire and summary, the personal coach emails and the shared-folder issue.
Timestamps make it easy to verify and navigate.
weaknesses: Does not list the marketing expert's promised email, nor the explicit per-role concept assignments as action items with owners.

evaluations.label: D
errors: 'Target group 15-35 years' is stated as a decision; the group explicitly did not settle on an age range and moved toward defining objectives and income instead.
'Investigate technical feasibility for rechargeable battery' is presented as an action item; it was only a suggestion that the group should maybe investigate whether a battery is needed.
Many timestamps are off or approximate (for example 04:50, 06:26, 23:39 and 28:55 do not match the matching content).
strengths: Compact and scannable, with the main numbers correct (75%, 80%, 10%, over 50% losing remotes, 12.50 production cost).
Records the infrared choice, the four components, the no-teletext rule, the TV-only scope and the yellow/black colors.
Has a short action list, labeled unassigned.
weaknesses: Very terse; leaves out the 25 euro price rationale, RSI, the sliding hatch discussion and the reasoning behind decisions.
Misses the individual assignments, the questionnaire and summary, and the project manager's documentation follow-ups.
Presents an unresolved target group as decided.

rationale: C is the most accurate and the most useful: it keeps the target market open as the transcript does, gives the reasoning behind the voice-recognition and secondary-button decisions, and lists owned follow-ups for the project manager. A is close and covers most content well, but its action item about the working-design presentation reverses who was missing a file and its next steps are generic and unowned. D is short and wrongly treats a 15-35 target group as decided, and it misses most of the closing assignments, though it does include some action items. B has well-organized sections but no action items, misattributes the voice-recognition decision to management, invents unresolved questions, and uses opaque speaker numbers.
